messages:
maria: quick sync — i posted an RFC earlier about moving per-tenant credit leases into a consolidated lease service. sketching concerns before i iterate.

jon: high level pros: less write amp on ledger, single lifecycle for lease cleanup, simpler orphan detection. cons: new scale/sopoint and potential cross-tenant contention. also rollback semantics get trickier. :thinking:

sam: from compliance we need immutable attribution events with clear token lineage. any shared service must emit a deterministically keyed `lease_acquire` event so downstream reconcilers can prove who used tokens.

lee: latency concern — we can't block every request on an RPC. proposed pattern: runtimes emit a light-weight envelope locally and perform a small optimistic prefetch; shared lease service reconciles async and emits final events. example envelope: 

```
{"envelope_version":"1","claim_id":"uuid-1234","tenant_id":"tid-42","tokens_requested":"50","local_prefetch":"10","lineage":"[request_id,proxy_id]","trace_ctx":"trace-abc","timestamp":"2026-03-10T14:12:00Z"}
```

lee: local_prefetch keeps p95 latency low. shared service will produce `lease_acquired` or `lease_denied` audit events.

maria: fallback if lease service unreachable? and how to avoid double-counting if local prefetch used then denied later?

jon: options: (a) local ephemeral lease with short TTL + mark `fallback=true` in audit; (b) route to degraded capacity model; (c) fail fast. i'm leaning (a) + compensating events, but we must define SLA for reconciler window.

sam: to prevent double-counting compensations must be first-class. local prefetch => emit `prefetch_claim` with claim_id; if denied later reconciler emits `prefetch_revoke` with same claim_id. billing treats revoke as negative entry during reconciliation windows. dedupe by claim_id.

lee: implementation: commitlog topic keyed by tenant for ordering; reconciler consumes full topic and writes compacted balancing entries. use claim_id as dedupe key. keep small windowed state for pending prefetches to speed decisions.

maria: sounds like two interfaces to formalize: (1) runtime -> lease API (fast accept/revoke + prefetch) and (2) lease -> audit/ledger (immutable, ordered, dedup-able). we should draft event contracts.

jon: also add metrics: prefetch_accept_rate, prefetch_revoke_rate, reconcile_lag, claim_dedupe_rate. alerts on spike in revoke vs accept.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for `lease-service-v1` in us-west-2 (canary=3 pods). logs -> https://logs.internal/lease-service/6877771234 :eyes:

sam: auditors want at least 90 days per-token provenance; enterprise customers may require 1 year. audit topic must be durable/compacted and we should plan an archive (S3) for older proofs.

lee: trade: per-tenant virtual shards in the lease service vs shared keying in a single store. shards give predictable tail but complicate migration and resharding. leaning shards initially to avoid noisy neighbors.

maria: action items: jon -> write fallback semantics + reconciler SLA; lee -> event contract for `prefetch_claim`/`lease_acquired`/`prefetch_revoke` + sample compacted ledger layout; sam -> draft compliance retention + archive workflow; i'll run perf spike for local_prefetch=10/20/50 and post results.

jon: quick q for sam: minimum retention auditors accept? 90 days or 1 year?

sam: NA/EU minimal 90d, enterprise might ask 1y. include both in plan.

lee: i'll drop a strawman event contract tomorrow. leaning virtual shards to start.

maria: thanks all. tagging RFC followup board. :thumbsup:
